“I just think it’s sweet.”

He reached over and tucked a strand of hair behind her ear.

“It’s true.”

She smiled.

Then the video reached the final question, where she’d guessed his favourite little luxury.

Xiaoran suddenly sat upright.

“Wait!”

Yichen looked at her.

“What?”

“I forgot something.”

“What?”

She picked up her phone and opened the comments.

There were already thousands.

People were praising their chemistry, laughing at the little exchanges, and pointing out how naturally Yichen watched Xiaoran whenever she spoke.

One comment caught her attention:

The way he doesn’t just know her favourite things, but understands WHY she likes them. That’s the real green flag.

She read it aloud.

Yichen glanced at the screen.

“That’s nice.”

Xiaoran scrolled further.

Another comment said:

Four years together and he still looks at her like he’s learning something new about her.

She stopped.

Then she turned toward him.

“Yichen.”

“Hmm?”

“Do you really think you still have things to learn about me?”

He looked at her for a moment.

“Of course.”

“Like what?”

He put his phone aside.

“What’s something you’ve wanted to try recently but haven’t told me?”

Xiaoran blinked.

She hadn’t expected him to turn the question around.

“That’s not fair.”

“Why?”

“Because now I have to think.”

He waited.

She looked up at the ceiling, thinking.

Then her eyes brightened.

“I want to learn ice skating.”

Yichen nodded.

“Ice skating?”

“Yes. I saw a video of a couple skating backwards holding hands. I want to try.”

“Then we can go.”

She smiled.

“Really?”

“Find a place you like.”

She leaned against his shoulder.

“And I want to try making pasta from scratch.”

“All right.”

“And maybe learn how to play tennis.”

He glanced down at her.

“Anything else?”

She thought for a moment.

“Actually, I want to go somewhere we’ve never been. Not a big trip. Just somewhere neither of us knows.”

Yichen nodded.

“Then we’ll do that too.”

She looked up at him.

“You’re making a list now?”

“I’m listening.”

Xiaoran smiled and wrapped her arms around his waist.

“You know, I think that’s my favourite thing about you.”

“What?”

“You never make me feel silly for wanting to try something.”

His expression softened.

He lowered his head and kissed her forehead.

“You don’t need a reason to want something.”

She looked at him.

“Even if it’s something random?”

“Especially then.”

She laughed quietly and settled against him again.

On the television, the video continued playing, the credits rolling beneath a final shot of them laughing together.

Mai Lang’s title card appeared:

HOW WELL DO YOU KNOW YOUR PARTNER? — ZHOU YICHEN & LIN XIAORAN

They had scored ten to nine, and she was never going to let him forget the pasta.

But as Xiaoran rested her head against his chest, she thought that perhaps the best part wasn’t knowing each other’s favourite drinks, ideal weekends, or preferred gifts.

It was knowing that even after four years, there were still new things to discover.

And Yichen, who had quietly begun searching for ice rinks on his phone, seemed to agree.

synopsis.title: Synopsis
synopsis.content:
Lin Xiaoran is loud, dramatic, cries easily, and can get lost walking somewhere she’s been twenty times. Zhou Yichen is calm, patient, and very hard not to notice. He fell for her almost right away, and he has been spoiling her ever since.

From their last years of high school to university in Shanghai, The Softest Kind of Love follows the two of them through first dates and bad fights, exams and families, and the slow work of growing up without growing apart.

Main chapters tell the story in order. Side stories are small moments you can read whenever you like.

contentWarn.title: Content Warning
contentWarn.content:
This is a gentle romance, but a few chapters include:

• A crude, sexualized remark made about Xiaoran by a classmate (The One Time Zhou Yichen Lost His Temper)

• A physical fight between students (Xiaoran, Don’t Fight)

• A sports injury with some blood and a hospital visit (Don’t Scare Me Like That Again, Don’t Limp. I’ll Cry Again.)

• Hurtful rumors and a brief break-up scare (Should We Break Up?)

• Dieting and skipped meals after hurtful online comments (The Day Zhou Yichen Found Out Lin Xiaoran Was Dieting)

• Mild language and lots of crying

authorNote.title: Author Note
authorNote.content:
I wanted to write the kind of love story I like to read before bed: no cheating, no misunderstanding that drags on for twenty chapters, nobody secretly dying. Just two people who like each other a lot and keep choosing each other, even on the days one of them is being impossible.

Xiaoran is a bit of everyone who has cried over a math test or sulked because their boyfriend was too popular. Yichen is the person a lot of us wish we had, or wish we were—someone who notices when you’ve gone quiet.

Some chapters are silly. Some are soft. A couple of them made me cry a little while writing. Thank you for reading any of them at all.

— 甜慕
